# PRD -- Slice 9: Tenancy & Patient Roster

Sprint: Phase 3 / Workstream Platform
Status: Proposed (2026-07-19)
Ticket handle: PAXOS-S9-TENANCY
Owner: Platform Engineering
Last updated: 2026-07-19

================================================================================
1. PROBLEM SUMMARY
================================================================================

P7a (ADR-0017, live 2026-07-18) established the schema foundation for
multi-tenancy: tenant_id and patient_ref fields ride every case-bearing object,
sessions carry a tenant_id claim, and both read endpoints enforce a
fail-closed TenancyScope at the store query boundary. However, several
consequential pieces remain deferred to the Phase 3 durable store milestone:

1. No real multi-tenant data isolation. A single seeded tenant (tenant_demo)
   is in place. Bearer callers are "platform-plane" (see all tenants), but
   there is only one tenant to see. No API surface exists to create or manage
   tenants.

2. No patient roster / panel management. patient_ref is a tokenized working
   identifier (PT-XXXX, ADR-0014) but there is no patient record, no
   user->patient panel assignment, and no roster API. Coordinators cannot
   associate a case with a named patient record.

3. No role claim on sessions. The session carries tenant_id but not a role
   (Operate / Build / Scale / Sponsor). Role-gated UI views are demo-only;
   the backend does not enforce them.

4. Panel scoping (O9) -- a session sees only its own assigned patient panel --
   is explicitly deferred (doc 10, P7a section).

5. Break-glass PHI access (gap G5 / unit O13) requires a user identity to
   attribute; without role + panel, the prerequisite is absent.

This slice completes the multi-tenancy model through the durable store layer,
introduces the patient roster, wires role onto sessions, and establishes
panel-scoped read paths -- the minimum viable multi-tenant runtime needed
before break-glass and real payer connector work can land.

================================================================================
2. GOALS
================================================================================

1. Introduce a durable tenant + user store (PostgreSQL) replacing the
   in-memory session store and the single-seeded-tenant pre-DB placeholders.
   The AuditRecord list also moves to PostgreSQL in this slice (per ADR-0009
   note and the Phase 3 milestone in doc 10).

2. Implement a patient roster model: PatientRecord (PT-token, demographics
   stub, assigned panel), Panel (org-scoped patient list), and the
   user->panel assignment that makes panel-scoped read paths possible.

3. Add role: UserRole to the session token and enforce it at the route level
   for role-gated endpoints (Operate / Build / Scale / Sponsor).

4. Implement panel-scoped read paths for /api/audit/records and
   /api/reviews/pending: an Operate session sees only its own assigned
   patients' cases; a Build/Scale session sees all tenant cases; Sponsor sees
   only suppressed aggregates.

5. Add a GET /api/patients endpoint returning the caller's panel
   (Operate-only; other roles 403).

6. Add POST /api/admin/tenants + GET /api/admin/tenants management surface
   (platform-plane Bearer only).

7. Migrate the InMemorySaver LangGraph checkpointer to a PostgreSQLSaver
   (shared asyncpg pool), completing the ADR-0010 Phase 3 note.

8. Ensure the TenancyScope fail-closed invariant (ADR-0017 standing
   invariant #6) survives the store migration -- acceptance tests written in
   P7a become the green suite for this slice.

================================================================================
3. NON-GOALS
================================================================================

- Break-glass PHI access (O13). This slice creates the prerequisite (user
  identity with role); the break-glass UI and AuditRecord reason class are the
  next slice.
- SAML/OIDC SSO. Sessions remain username/password; SSO is a future
  connector.
- Billing / subscription management. Tenant records carry only the identifiers
  needed for data scoping.
- EHR patient-sync. PatientRecord is created via API; no live EHR pull in
  this slice.
- Langfuse trace emission. Deferred (ADR-0007).
- Changes to the appeal or initial-PA pipeline topology. Tenancy is a
  cross-cutting concern; the pipelines themselves are not changed.

================================================================================
4. REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

Functional
----------

T-1  PostgreSQL replaces the in-memory audit/store.py list. AuditRecord rows
     are written before the terminal SSE event per ADR-0009 (durability rule
     now enforced at the DB write, not a list append). Idempotency key
     uniqueness is a DB unique constraint.

T-2  PostgreSQL replaces security/sessions.py. Sessions are rows with a 30-min
     TTL enforced at read. A new asyncpg connection pool is the shared
     primitive; routes are unchanged (same cookie/CSRF contract).

T-3  PostgreSQLSaver (from langgraph-checkpoint-postgres) replaces
     InMemorySaver for the appeal graph checkpointer. thread_id =
     correlation_id semantics are unchanged. is_run_parked uses the same
     public _PIPELINE.get_state(config).next check.

T-4  A tenants table tracks: tenant_id (UUID PK), name, created_at.
     Platform-plane Bearer callers only can POST /api/admin/tenants (create)
     and GET /api/admin/tenants (list).

T-5  A users table tracks: user_id, tenant_id (FK), username, role: UserRole,
     hashed_password, created_at. POST /api/admin/users creates a user within
     a tenant (platform-plane or tenant-admin role).

T-6  UserRole enum: operate, build, scale, sponsor, tenant_admin,
     platform_admin. Added to schemas.py with TypeScript parity.

T-7  Session token gains role: UserRole stamped at login from the users table.
     Auth middleware resolves it onto request.state.role.

T-8  PatientRecord table: patient_ref (PT-XXXX token, PK), tenant_id (FK),
     panel_id (FK, nullable), demographics_stub (JSONB -- synthetic-only in
     this slice, drawn from IDENTITY_POOL), created_at.

T-9  Panel table: panel_id (UUID PK), tenant_id (FK), name, user_ids (JSONB
     array). A user assigned to a panel sees only that panel's patients in
     Operate-role read paths.

T-10 /api/audit/records and /api/reviews/pending apply panel scoping:
     - operate role  -> filter by patient_ref IN panel.patient_refs
     - build/scale   -> all tenant records
     - sponsor       -> aggregate counts only (n >= 11 suppression)
     - platform Bearer -> all tenants

T-11 GET /api/patients returns the caller's panel's PatientRecord list
     (Operate-only; Build/Scale/Sponsor get 403; platform-plane Bearer gets
     all tenants' patients).

T-12 All DB queries use parameterized statements; no string interpolation of
     user-supplied values into SQL.

T-13 DB connection pool is initialized at app startup (lifespan handler in
     main.py); routes get the pool via request.app.state.db_pool. No
     per-request connection construction.

Non-functional
--------------

T-14 The TenancyScope fail-closed invariant holds post-migration: all
     acceptance tests from P7a pass against the new PostgreSQL-backed store.

T-15 AuditRecord write before terminal event: P99 write latency <= 100 ms
     (local PostgreSQL); circuit breaker wraps the pool to degrade gracefully
     if the DB is unreachable (error event, not a silent drop).

T-16 Migrations are managed by alembic; alembic upgrade head is idempotent.
     A clean-state test database is created in CI using a fixture, not the
     production schema.

T-17 PHI in PatientRecord.demographics_stub is behind the tokenization boundary
     (ADR-0014): the JSONB stores tokens ({{PATIENT_NAME}}), not direct
     identifiers. Rehydration happens only at Operate-role egress.

================================================================================
5. WORKFLOW MODELING
================================================================================

Session login (updated)
------------------------

  POST /api/auth/login { username, password }
          |
          v
  users table lookup (constant-time compare, asyncpg)
  |-- not found / wrong password -> 401
  +-- found -> { user_id, tenant_id, role }
          |
          v
  sessions table INSERT
  (session_id, user_id, tenant_id, role, csrf_token, expires_at)
          |
          v
  Set-Cookie: paxos_session=<session_id> (httpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict)
  Response: { user_id, csrf_token, role }

Audit record write (updated, durable)
--------------------------------------

  AuditBoundary.with_audit(...)
          |
          v
  INSERT INTO audit_records (...)
  ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING
          | (written BEFORE terminal SSE event)
          v
  DoneEvent / ErrorEvent emitted

Panel-scoped read path
-----------------------

  GET /api/audit/records
          |
          v
  auth_middleware -> request.state.tenancy_scope, request.state.role
          |
          v
  TenancyScope.build_filter(role):
  |-- platform_admin / Bearer  -> no tenant filter
  |-- tenant_admin / build / scale -> WHERE tenant_id = $1
  |-- operate -> WHERE tenant_id = $1
  |               AND patient_ref = ANY($2::text[])
  |               ($2 = panel.patient_refs for caller's panel)
  +-- sponsor -> aggregate only (COUNT per drug/denial_reason, suppress n < 11)
          |
          v
  SELECT * FROM audit_records WHERE <filter>
          |
          v
  AuditRecordsResponse (or AggregateResponse for Sponsor)

================================================================================
6. DATA MODEL CHANGES
================================================================================

New database schema (alembic/versions/)
-----------------------------------------

  -- tenants
  CREATE TABLE tenants (
      tenant_id  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      name       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  );

  -- users
  CREATE TABLE users (
      user_id       UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      tenant_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(tenant_id),
      username      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      role          TEXT NOT NULL,
      password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
      created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  );

  -- sessions (replaces in-memory store)
  CREATE TABLE sessions (
      session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
      tenant_id  UUID NOT NULL,
      role       TEXT NOT NULL,
      csrf_token TEXT NOT NULL,
      expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
  );
  CREATE INDEX sessions_expires_at ON sessions(expires_at);

  -- audit_records (replaces in-memory list)
  CREATE TABLE audit_records (
      id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
      correlation_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
      idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      tenant_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
      patient_ref     TEXT,
      lifecycle       TEXT NOT NULL,
      created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
      -- ... all AuditRecord fields as columns ...
  );
  CREATE INDEX audit_tenant_idx  ON audit_records(tenant_id);
  CREATE INDEX audit_patient_idx ON audit_records(patient_ref);

  -- patients
  CREATE TABLE patients (
      patient_ref  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
      tenant_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(tenant_id),
      panel_id     UUID,
      demographics JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
      created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  );

  -- panels
  CREATE TABLE panels (
      panel_id  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(tenant_id),
      name      TEXT NOT NULL,
      user_ids  JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb
  );

New Python models (backend/models/schemas.py)
----------------------------------------------

  class UserRole(str, Enum):
      operate        = "operate"
      build          = "build"
      scale          = "scale"
      sponsor        = "sponsor"
      tenant_admin   = "tenant_admin"
      platform_admin = "platform_admin"

  class PatientRecord(BaseModel):
      patient_ref  : str
      tenant_id    : str
      panel_id     : str | None
      demographics : dict    # tokenized JSONB; rehydrated at egress only

  class Panel(BaseModel):
      panel_id  : str
      tenant_id : str
      name      : str
      user_ids  : list[str]

  class TenantRecord(BaseModel):
      tenant_id  : str
      name       : str
      created_at : datetime

  class LoginResponse(BaseModel):     # extended (was {user_id, csrf_token})
      user_id    : str
      csrf_token : str
      role       : UserRole

Parity: UserRole mirrors into src/types.ts. LoginResponse.role added.
wire-types-freshness CI job catches any drift.

================================================================================
7. API CHANGES
================================================================================

Modified endpoints
------------------

POST /api/auth/login    -- response gains role: UserRole.

GET /api/audit/records  -- panel-scoped filtering by role (see workflow above).
                           sponsor role returns AggregateAuditResponse.

GET /api/reviews/pending -- panel-scoped: operate sees only own panel's parked
                            runs.

New endpoints
-------------

POST /api/admin/tenants
  Auth    : Platform-plane Bearer only (403 for any cookie session).
  Body    : { name: str }
  Response: TenantRecord

GET /api/admin/tenants
  Auth    : Platform-plane Bearer only.
  Response: { tenants: TenantRecord[] }

POST /api/admin/users
  Auth    : Platform-plane or tenant_admin role.
  Body    : { username, password, role, tenant_id }
  Response: { user_id, tenant_id, role }

GET /api/patients
  Auth    : operate role only (403 for other roles; platform Bearer returns all
            tenants).
  Response: { patients: PatientRecord[] }

POST /api/patients
  Auth    : tenant_admin or platform-plane.
  Body    : { patient_ref, panel_id?, demographics? }
  Response: PatientRecord

Removed / replaced
------------------

security/sessions.py in-memory store -> PostgreSQL sessions table. No API
contract change; paxos_session cookie semantics are identical.

================================================================================
8. LANGGRAPH INTEGRATION
================================================================================

Checkpointer migration (agents/graph.py)
-----------------------------------------

  # Before (P7a)
  from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
  checkpointer = InMemorySaver()

  # After (S9)
  from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres.aio import AsyncPostgresSaver
  checkpointer = AsyncPostgresSaver(conn=app.state.db_pool)
  _PIPELINE = workflow.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)

- thread_id = correlation_id semantics are unchanged.
- is_run_parked(correlation_id) continues to use
  _PIPELINE.get_state(config).next -- the public API survives the checkpointer
  swap (this is the explicit design in ADR-0010).
- langgraph-checkpoint-postgres must pass the ADR-0007 pre-install protocol
  before landing; it is a first-party LangGraph package, but the protocol
  applies uniformly.

No pipeline topology change
----------------------------

The appeal and initial-PA graph structures are unaffected. Tenancy is enforced
at the API boundary and the store query layer, not inside LangGraph nodes.

================================================================================
9. NEW MODULES
================================================================================

  backend/
  |-- db/
  |   |-- __init__.py
  |   |-- pool.py           # asyncpg pool factory (init at lifespan)
  |   |-- audit_store.py    # PostgreSQL-backed AuditStore
  |   |-- session_store.py  # PostgreSQL-backed SessionStore
  |   |-- tenant_store.py   # Tenant + User CRUD
  |   +-- patient_store.py  # PatientRecord + Panel CRUD
  +-- alembic/
      |-- env.py
      +-- versions/
          +-- 0001_initial_schema.py

audit/store.py is NOT deleted in this slice -- it is kept as a fallback adapter
that the AuditStore Protocol wraps, to allow the pre-DB path to be exercised
in unit tests with MockAuditStore. The live app wires the PostgreSQL-backed
store at startup.

AuditStore Protocol:

  class AuditStore(Protocol):
      async def write(self, record: AuditRecord) -> None: ...
      async def all_records(self, scope: TenancyScope) -> list[AuditRecord]: ...
      async def pending_reviews(
          self, scope: TenancyScope, is_parked: Callable
      ) -> list[PendingReview]: ...

================================================================================
10. UI SURFACES
================================================================================

Role-gated view binding
------------------------

src/capabilities.ts manifest gains a requiredRole field per unit (e.g.,
{ unit: "O6", requiredRole: "operate" }). The session gate in the single-shell
migration reads request.state.role (now returned by GET /api/auth/me) and hides
units whose requiredRole the caller does not hold.

GET /api/auth/me response is extended: { user_id, role } (additive change).

Patient roster view (new, Operate-role)
----------------------------------------

A new capability unit O9 (patient panel / roster) backed by GET /api/patients
appears in the capability manifest as live. It renders the panel's
PatientRecord list with PT-token display and a link to open the case queue
filtered to that patient.

PHI rehydration: the Operate-role egress replaces {{PATIENT_NAME}} tokens with
values from the IDENTITY_POOL lookup at render time; the API returns tokens
only.

================================================================================
11. TEST CASES
================================================================================

Unit (backend/tests/unit/)
---------------------------

Module: test_db_audit_store.py
  - Write idempotency (same idempotency_key inserts once)
  - all_records respects TenancyScope
  - panel filter returns only panel patients
  - sponsor role returns aggregate counts with n < 11 suppression

Module: test_db_session_store.py
  - Session created, read, and expired correctly
  - expired session returns None
  - CSRF token comparison is constant-time

Module: test_user_role_parity.py
  - UserRole enum in schemas.py and src/types.ts are identical

Module: test_tenant_store.py
  - Tenant creation idempotent on name
  - user created with role
  - wrong tenant_id rejected by FK

Module: test_patient_store.py
  - PatientRecord created with PT token
  - panel assignment updates panel.user_ids
  - panel-scoped query returns correct subset

Module: test_tenancy_scope.py (extend P7a suite)
  - All P7a acceptance tests pass against PostgreSQL-backed store
    (use pytest-asyncio + pytest-postgresql fixture)

Contract
--------

test_schema_parity.py extended: UserRole in both sides.
test_schema_parity.py: LoginResponse.role field present in MeResponse.

Integration (backend/tests/integration/)
-----------------------------------------

Module: test_auth_with_db.py
  - Login returns role
  - session persists across requests
  - expired session 401
  - logout removes session

Module: test_panel_scoped_reads.py
  - Operate session sees only own panel's records
  - Build session sees all tenant records
  - Sponsor session sees only aggregate
  - platform Bearer sees all tenants

Module: test_admin_endpoints.py
  - POST /api/admin/tenants (Bearer only)
  - cookie session 403
  - GET /api/patients (operate only)
  - build role 403

Module: test_audit_durability.py
  - AuditRecord written before DoneEvent (timing assertion via DB query after
    SSE stream ends)
  - idempotent write on duplicate idempotency_key

Module: test_checkpointer_migration.py
  - Exception-tier run parks at PostgreSQLSaver checkpoint
  - resume retrieves checkpoint
  - is_run_parked returns correct boolean

CI environment
--------------

  - Add services: postgres: image: postgres:16 to backend-unit and
    backend-integration CI jobs.
  - Alembic upgrade head runs as a CI setup step before integration tests.
  - POSTGRES_DSN env var set in CI from the GitHub Actions service container.

================================================================================
12. RISKS
================================================================================

Risk: PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion under concurrent SSE streams
  Likelihood: Medium | Impact: High
  Mitigation: Pool size configurable via DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE env var (default 10);
  circuit breaker wraps pool acquisition.

Risk: langgraph-checkpoint-postgres not yet through ADR-0007 pre-install review
  Likelihood: Medium | Impact: Medium
  Mitigation: Ship the InMemorySaver->PostgreSQLSaver swap as a separate
  sub-slice gated on ADR-0007 clearance; audit store migration can land first.

Risk: Panel-scoped filter returning empty set for Operate user with no panel
  Likelihood: Low | Impact: Medium
  Mitigation: Empty list is valid (user has no assigned patients); UI shows
  "no patients assigned" state.

Risk: Alembic migration failures in production rollback
  Likelihood: Low | Impact: High
  Mitigation: All migrations are reversible (downgrade); staging environment
  runs migration before production.

Risk: demographics_stub JSONB stores direct identifier by mistake
  Likelihood: Medium | Impact: High
  Mitigation: CI test_golden_compliance.py scan extended to cover PatientRecord
  test fixtures; rehydration helper is the only place that resolves tokens.
